findings.evidence: #s3-step3 style="order:3" ("Confirm your order") precedes #s3-step2 style="order:2" ("Enter payment details") precedes #s3-step1 style="order:1" ("Choose a plan") in DOM order
findings.violation: DOM order presents the steps as Confirm your order, then Enter payment details, then Choose a plan, the reverse of the sequence the order property (3, 2, 1) declares for visual placement, so a linearized reading receives the confirmation step before the two steps it depends on.
findings.fix: Reorder the three .step elements in the markup to match the intended completion sequence (Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order), or remove the order property and rely on source order alone.

findings.evidence: The page exposes one navigation mechanism, #nav with links "Plan a trip" and "Service alerts"; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere in the document.
findings.violation: Fewer than two independent navigation mechanisms are present, and the page's content is a general service-update article, not one step in a linear process exempted by the criterion.
findings.fix: Add a second independent mechanism, such as a site search form, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail, alongside the existing primary navigation.

findings.evidence: , no role, tabindex, or accessible name attribute on the div
findings.violation: A custom control built from a div, named by its own class as a delete action, carries no role, no programmatically determinable name, and no keyboard access; a screen reader exposes nothing at this location for a user to discover the control exists.
findings.fix: Use a native <button> element with a visible or aria-label accessible name (for example "Delete"), or add role="button", tabindex="0", a keyboard handler, and an aria-label to the div.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>, the only field label in the form styled with a non-default text color
findings.violation: The Phone number label is distinguished from the form's other three labels only by red text color, with no accompanying text, icon, or symbol carrying the same signal.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal alongside the red styling, such as a "(required)" text suffix or an asterisk with an accessible equivalent, or remove the color-only distinction if it carries no meaning.

findings.evidence: Heading text "Accessibility improvements" is followed by #s1-p1 ("Riders may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app...") and #s1-p2 ("Passengers can check real time arrivals by calling rider services..."), neither of which describes an accessibility improvement; only the section's image, #s1-img1, relates to accessibility.
findings.violation: The heading's wording promises accessibility-specific content, but two of the section's three items describe an unrelated fare-adjustment and arrivals process, so a reader scanning headings for accessibility information is misled about what most of the section actually covers.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match the fare-adjustment and arrivals content it actually introduces, or move that content under a heading that already covers it and keep this heading for genuinely accessibility-related content.

findings.violation: The only error text associated with the invalid Promo code field reads "Error.", a generic phrase that does not state what is wrong with the entered value.
findings.fix: Replace the error text with a specific description, for example "Promo code not recognized, check for typos or an expired code."
